result.headline: Pitch loop on UAV-09 does not track its setpoint, while roll follows with lag; cause not isolated.
result.explanation: A control fault shows in pitch: attitude correlates negatively with setpoint (-0.364; -0.72 at 0.975 s lag) and the elevator output ch[2] saturates. Roll tracks with a 1.219 s lag. A Sensor health error and Low voltage warning appear at t=1.083.

evidence.quote: TRACKING control.attitude_setpoint[pitch] vs vehicle.attitude[pitch]: typical |error| 9.499 deg, worst 47.355 at t=71.583 s; 6 window(s) above 28.498
evidence.shows: Pitch is the worst-tracked axis. Correlation with the setpoint is -0.364, and -0.72 at a 0.975 s lag, so the response is inverted or badly delayed.

evidence.quote: TRACKING control.attitude_setpoint[roll] vs vehicle.attitude[roll]: typical |error| 5.245 deg, worst 42.971 at t=7.285 s; 6 window(s) above 15.734
evidence.shows: Roll follows its setpoint with correlation 0.965 at a 1.219 s lag. The large roll error is mostly this lag, not a lost axis.

evidence.quote: EVENT t=1.083 s controller.event[mavros: System] mavros: System: ERROR: Sensor helth
evidence.shows: A sensor-health error and a Low voltage warning (line 22) appear together at t=1.083, before any tracking divergence.

evidence.quote: CHANGE actuator.output[ch[2]] at t=91.667 s: 1428 -> 1100 us (step -328, 41x its usual variation)
evidence.shows: The ch[2] output swings between its limits of 1100 and 1700 us. From 66.7 to 68.646 s it is held at 1700 while the pitch setpoint is mostly negative-to-positive and the attitude rises.

evidence.quote: ANOMALY a4 t=6.414 s: vehicle.attitude[roll] did not follow control.attitude_setpoint[roll] (peak |error| 42.971)
evidence.shows: In the roll event, ch[3-5] moved at 6.002 s, before the attitude left baseline at 7.671 s. The outputs respond to the setpoint and the attitude responds later.

checked.check: Order of first deviations in the roll event at 5.5-9.5 s
checked.result: Setpoint left baseline at 5.997 s, attitude at 7.671 s, ch[1] at 7.694 s. ch[3-5] stepped at 6.002 s (lines 34, 37, 40).
checked.about: Roll axis responds with a delay and no loss of authority, so it is the weaker candidate.

checked.check: Order of first deviations in the pitch event at 62.5-73 s
checked.result: Pitch and yaw setpoints moved first (62.528 s). Throttle, ch[1] and ch[2] followed at 62.664 to 62.702 s. Attitude pitch moved at 63.555 s.
checked.about: The actuators respond to the setpoint. The attitude response is late or inverted.

checked.check: Setpoint vs attitude relation, roll and pitch
checked.result: Roll: correlation 0.965 at a 1.219 s lag. Pitch: -0.364 overall, -0.72 at a 0.975 s lag.
checked.about: A pitch control or sign fault is more likely than a roll fault.

checked.result: ch[2] stays at 1700 us from 66.7 to 68.646 s with the throttle at 75%. The pitch setpoint goes from -15.9 at 66.603 s to 17.44 at 68.4 s while the attitude climbs to 10.379 at 67.269 s.
checked.about: Elevator saturation or an inverted pitch response.

effects.quote: ANOMALY a1 t=2.341 s: vehicle.attitude[pitch] stepped -22.008 -> 11.904 deg (see line 58; strength 2.975)
effects.why: Large attitude steps follow setpoint or sensor changes. The 0.244 s sample interval with held values makes them look like jumps.

effects.quote: ANOMALY a9 t=63.555 s: vehicle.velocity[x] stepped 14.62 -> 0.425 m/s (see line 69; strength 3.015)
effects.why: Velocity and airspeed steps follow the attitude disturbance and are not the earliest sign.
The yaw error is large and constant. This looks like a frame or reference offset between setpoint and attitude, not a fault in flight.

next_action.action: Bench-check pitch sign and elevator direction with the aircraft restrained
next_action.why: Separates a pitch control/sign or actuator fault from an attitude-sensor or estimator fault, and from the delay seen in roll.
how: Props off or motor disarmed, aircraft held level.
Tilt the nose up and note whether ch[2] moves the elevator the stabilising way.
Command a pitch setpoint step and compare the elevator travel with its limits, 1100-1700 us.
Read the sensor-health status and battery voltage at rest.
next_action.conditions: Aircraft restrained, props off, fully charged battery, on the bench, same firmware as flight-09.
next_action.baseline: The roll axis in this recording, which tracks at correlation 0.965 with a 1.219 s lag.

outcomes.label: Elevator moves the wrong way
outcomes.means: Pitch control sign or mixing fault. Pitch loop is the main cause.
outcomes.then: Inspect pitch mixer and servo reversal settings.

outcomes.label: Elevator correct; attitude estimate wrong
outcomes.means: Attitude sensor or estimator fault, consistent with the Sensor health error.
outcomes.then: Request sensor logs and a calibration check.

outcomes.label: All correct on bench; low battery persists
outcomes.means: Power sag or tuning is more likely. Check voltage under load.
outcomes.then: Request battery voltage log for the flight.

unknowns: The recording has no battery voltage or current series, so Low voltage cannot be tied to the tracking errors.
Yaw tracking error cannot be judged: yaw_rate is constant 0 and the setpoint and attitude references differ.
It is unclear whether the roll lag of 1.219 s is real response delay or a logging time offset.

already_answered.question: Did a control fault occur, and when?
already_answered.answer: Earliest pitch divergence starts at 0.398 s, roll at 6.414 s. The worst pitch error is 47.355 deg at 71.583 s.

already_answered.question: Where on the aircraft: which control channel?
already_answered.answer: Most likely pitch, through the elevator on ch[2]. Roll tracks with a lag. ch[0], ch[6] and ch[7] are constant.

data_requests.what: Battery voltage and current, IMU and estimator health for this flight
data_requests.why_needed: Separates the Sensor health and Low voltage warnings from a pitch control fault.

unobservable.fact: Servo reversal, linkage direction and mixer settings for the elevator
unobservable.why_it_matters: A reversed or mis-mixed elevator would explain the negative pitch correlation.
unobservable.how_to_observe: Move the elevator by hand or with a pitch command on the bench and check its direction.

hypotheses.claim: Pitch control has a sign, mixing or saturation fault in the elevator on ch[2].
hypotheses.because: Pitch correlation is -0.364 (-0.72 at a 0.975 s lag). ch[2] sits at 1700 us from 66.7 to 68.646 s while pitch rises against the setpoint.
hypotheses.observed_at: commanded actuator output and the attitude estimate

hypotheses.claim: A sensor or estimator fault gives a wrong or delayed attitude, behind the Sensor health error.
hypotheses.because: The Sensor health error at t=1.083 and the held, stepped attitude samples fit this. No sensor raw data exists to test it.

hypotheses.claim: Low battery voltage limits actuator or motor performance.
hypotheses.because: Low voltage warning at 1.083 s. There is no voltage series, so no link to the tracking errors can be shown.

hypotheses.claim: The roll axis has lost authority.
hypotheses.because: Roll tracks with correlation 0.965 at a 1.219 s lag. The error is the lag, not lost authority.

hypotheses.claim: Timing offset between setpoint, outputs and attitude in the log produces the apparent lag.
hypotheses.because: The outputs move before the attitude. The attitude is logged slowly at 0.244 s with held values.
